newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed firmer, bouncing back from earlier lower levels after a surprise 0.3 percent fall in the May U.S. producer price index.
The fall in the PPI, which had been expected to show a month-on-month rise of 0.1 percent, was seen making a rise in U.S. interest rates less likely.
Dealers said business had been quiet, with institutional investors reluctant to buy into the bond market and apparently waiting for higher yields.

They said the final form of a stability pact on post-EMU budgetary discipline, due to be adopted at the EU's Amsterdam summit early next week, would be a key factor behind the direction of European bond markets.
A tough agreement would support prices, but a watered down deal would be negative, they said.

The short end of the curve saw some further flattening on Friday, with the spread between two and 10 years coming in to 190 basis points from 195 on Thursday and the 5-10 year spread narrowing to 96 basis points from 98.
